newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong stocks power on to close at record high.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks power on to close at record high.

text.p: Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index advanced 73.25 points to a record close of 12,510.05, on confident institutional and retail buying boosted by Wall Street's strong performance, brokers said on Friday.
The market opened firm and raced up more than 100 points before pausing, brokers said.
"We saw some intra-day profit-taking, then the market regained confidence to follow Wall Street's lead and move ahead, said one broker with a UK-based house.

Turnover was a strong HK$6.67 billion, compared with HK$6.87 billion on Thursday. Brokers noted heavy interest in Hopewell and Consolidated Electric Power Asia and in shares on which derivatives had been issued recently.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average surged 38 points on Thursday to a new record close of 6,059.
"We were a bit surprised at the market's strength today, but investors are confident on the market, at least for the short term," said Geoff Galbraith in institutional sales at NAVA SC Securities.
Some brokers attributed Hong Kong's strong performance in advance of a long holiday weekend to the poor performance of other regional markets.
"Hong Kong has good liquidity and short-term outlook and is attracting hot money from regional markets," said the UK broker.
The Hong Kong exchange will close for a local holiday on Monday, October 21.
Hopewell and CEPA led the most active table, after HSBC. Hopewell added HK$0.20 to HK$5.30 on heavy turnover of HK$406.32 million, while CEPA was unchanged at HK$17.90 on trade of HK$272.93 million.
Powering the Hang Seng to its new high was the finance sector, followed property shares.

HSBC added HK$2.00 to HK$155.00, after flirting with a new record high of HK$155.50 earlier in the day. Subsidiary Hang Seng Bank underwent profit-taking during the day, but managed to put on HK$0.25 at end to close at HK$93.00.
